note: Track major-on-neck (guitar-scales), step 3 (Dorian): position 1 of D Dorian seen on the whole neck, the crossing into position 2, the position over a D drone, then the same frets as position 3 of A Dorian over an A drone. Rewritten from the plan exercise (ChoiceSplit3): its Variant selector set a key and a position together, which a choice no longer does, so the two variants are two short sections, each with its own drone and neck. D is the lesson, so the block states no moves.

exercise.title: D Dorian on the neck
exercise.why: A mode is a shape counted from its root, so moving the root from A to D moves every position with it, and the 6th keeps its place inside each one.

cells.text:
The whole neck is drawn above the position, with position 1 of D Dorian framed on it. Play the position up and back down from the low {{1}}.
The ringed {{6}} is the note that makes the scale Dorian. Stay with the position until your fingers go to each {{6}} without a look.

The neck below shows only the crossing from position 1 to position 2 of D Dorian. Climb position 1 from the low {{1}}, and on the G string slide from {{4}} up to {{5}}: the rest of the climb is in position 2. Come back down the same way.
If the slide lands short, play only its two notes until your finger knows the distance.

Press Play below to start the drone on D. Play position 1 up and back down over it, and end on a ringed {{1}}.
Stop on a ringed {{6}} now and then, and listen to it against the drone.

Press Play below to start the drone, now on A. Your hand stays in the same frets: this is position 3 of A Dorian, where one note of the scale sits a fret higher. Play it up and back down, and end on a ringed {{1}}.
When you change the root, the frets under your hand stay and the ringed notes are in new places.
